result.summary: Native Windows builds and CI are migrated from MSVC (cl.exe) to LLVM's clang-cl driver, dropping support for compiling with cl.exe. CMake configuration, presets, warning flags, and documentation are updated for clang-cl, and builds are linked against Clang's builtins runtime library. Workarounds for MSVC-specific compiler bugs and constexpr limitations are removed.
result.problem: MSVC causes ongoing maintenance overhead due to compiler bugs and internal compiler errors (such as #31456 and #36153), lacks inline assembly support on x64 and ARM64 architectures, and produces slower binaries with longer CI compilation times than Clang.
evidence: Author benchmarks indicate block connection throughput increases significantly with clang-cl over MSVC (ConnectBlockAllEcdsa improves from 7.40 to 11.52 blocks/s; ConnectBlockAllSchnorr from 7.32 to 11.81 blocks/s).
Author reports Windows CI build times drop from 20m 35s under MSVC to 12m 43s under clang-cl.
Closes issue #31456 documenting MSVC internal compiler errors and allows removing an MSVC-specific static assertion workaround for issue #36153 in util_not_null_tests.cpp.

enables: Hardware-accelerated inline assembly on Windows (e.g. secp256k1 #1681)

result.scope_notes: This drops cl.exe support entirely rather than supporting both compilers simultaneously; native Windows developers must use the clang-cl toolset (available inside Visual Studio or LLVM).
result.changed_since_previous: Added suppressed CI compiler error flags for return-type and conditional-uninitialized warnings in ci-windows.py, and ensured bitcoinqt links against shlwapi on all Windows toolchains.
result.card: This pull request migrates native Windows builds and CI from MSVC (cl.exe) to clang-cl, dropping support for compiling with cl.exe. The switch resolves persistent MSVC-specific compiler bugs (#31456, #36153) and unblocks inline assembly optimizations on Windows. Author benchmarks show block connection performance improves by roughly 55% to 60%, and Windows CI run times drop from ~20 minutes to ~12 minutes. Native Windows developers will need the clang-cl toolset installed through Visual Studio or LLVM.

risk.why: Switching compiler toolchains and linking Clang runtime builtins on Windows could introduce compiler code-generation defects or break native Windows developer builds.
